name: Oregon
overview: Oregon pays qualifying senior and disabled homeowners’ property taxes through a repayable deferral.

programs.name: Property Tax Deferral for Disabled and Senior Homeowners
programs.ageRule: 62 or older, or receiving or eligible for Social Security Disability benefits.
programs.incomeDefinition: Prior-year household income, including taxable and nontaxable income under program rules.
programs.maximumBenefit: Eligible annual property taxes are paid by the state as a loan.
programs.formulaSummary: State pays the county; deferred taxes, 6% simple annual interest, and applicable costs must be repaid when the deferral ends.
programs.application: Apply through county assessor by April 15; late applications through December 1 require a fee.
eligibilityNotes: Generally five years of ownership and occupancy.
Property-value and mortgage requirements apply. The inventory does not establish the 2025 asset or insurance requirements.
programs.programYear: 2025 program enrollment; standard applications due April 15, 2025.

sources.title: Property Tax Deferral for Disabled and Senior Homeowners

laterChanges: 2026 enrollment raises the prior-year household-income limit to $70,000 and changes property-value rules.
researchNotes: Deferred taxes remain repayable with interest under the program rules.
The linked deferral sources do not establish an active Elderly Rental Assistance program for 2025.
